newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian stocks flat in listless summer trade.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian stocks flat in listless summer trade.

text.p: Norwegian shares were flat on Monday in modest turnover with the summer holidays in full swing. Dealers said the market lacked impulses from home and abroad, although investors were becoming slightly concerned about a recent rise in short-term interest rates.
"There is some uncertainty about (interest) rates in the Norwegian market for the time being and this is affecting the blue chips in general, with the exception opf Norsk Hydro," one dealer said.
Oslo's Total share index crept 0.07 pecent higher to close at 1,239.67 points in thin turnover of 571 million crowns.

Offshore services company Ocean Rig jumped 7.63 percent in 53 million crowns of business. Dealers said the move was based on a positive outlook for the rig market in general and on expectations that the company would soon seal a contract for its second rig.

Interest remained relatively high in the banking sector, with Den norske Bank and Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse in the top six of the most traded shares in value terms. DnB closed unchanged at 30.20 crowns in turnover of 40.6 million crowns, while Christiania ended almost two percent up at 26.40 crowns in trade worth 32 million crowns.
